s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic swelling and pain in the mastoid area with a calcified mass
salient_findings: Hyperostotic lesion of the outer table of the right calvarium
Densely calcified mass involving the inferior squamosal portion of the right temporal bone
Mild patchy internal enhancement and thickening of the inner table
key_facts: 28-year-old man with a history of migraine disorder
Several months of pain and swelling in the right mastoid area
Recent subjective enlargement of the mass and increased pain
Noncontrast CT showed a 3.0 × 3.0 × 1.1 cm hyperostotic lesion
MRI revealed a densely calcified mass measuring 3.6 × 1.5 × 3.0 cm
Low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images
Mild patchy internal enhancement
Thickening of the inner table
No soft-tissue component beyond the bone or dural involvement
Laboratory studies were within normal limits

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperostotic lesion with calcification, consistent with osteoma

shortlist.label: Osteoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Densely calcified mass with mild internal enhancement, possible osteoblastoma

shortlist.label: Ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Calcified mass with low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images, consistent with ossifying fibroma

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperostotic lesion with thickening of the inner table, possible fibrous dysplasia

shortlist.label: Osteoid osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Small, calcified mass with nocturnal pain, possible osteoid osteoma

raw.rationale: The presence of a hyperostotic lesion with dense calcification and low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images, along with mild patchy internal enhancement, is consistent with an osteoma. The lack of soft-tissue component or dural involvement also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Osteoblastoma
rejected.why: Osteoblastomas are typically larger and more aggressive than the lesion described, and often have a softer tissue component.

rejected.label: Ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Ossifying fibromas tend to have a more mixed signal intensity on MRI and may have a softer tissue component, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia often presents with a more ground-glass appearance on imaging and may have a larger area of involvement, which is not consistent with the focal lesion described.

rejected.label: Osteoid osteoma
rejected.why: Osteoid osteomas are typically smaller than the lesion described and often have a characteristic nidus with surrounding sclerosis, which is not seen in this case.
